en: The Glorious Hymn to the Serpent-Lord Mahānandīśvara

I perpetually bow to the innermost Liṅga of Great Bliss, whose supreme head is made beautiful by the crown, the moon, and the Gaṅgā; who is embraced by the body of Puṣpadantī from the eye on His forehead; and who is united with the Daughter of the Snowy Mountain.
I bow to the Liṅga that performs the cosmic dance upon the walls of the quarters starting from Indra, its limbs draped in the skin of the radiant elephant-hide.
I bow to the bee at the lotus-face of Gaurī, the Mother of the World.
I bow to Him who is known through the four Vedas, who is praised by the great Vedas, who is dear to the hearts of His bowing devotees, and who is attained through the grace of Murāri;
I bow to Him who has become the Guru and Brahman, whose nature is consciousness and bliss.

I bow to the bodiless one (Videha), who was consecrated upon the heads of Hari and Brahmā at the edge of the courtyard of the ancient city of Kāśī, where the banks were ploughed by the waves of the newly manifested celestial river (Gaṅgā); he who abandoned the host of enemies—
including friends, sons, prosperity, and the like— along with his great body that was fit for service.
I bow to the Lord of the gods, who rests upon the peak of the mountain within the midst of his massed matted locks; who is the great blissful Liṅga;
who is displayed with the magnanimity of a gatekeeper at the four gates; who is devoted to the heart-stealing songs of the Gandharvas; and who performs a sublime dance. (5–6)
